scenes.audio: Marcus is applying for a life policy. The producer asks the questions on the approved application, records his answers, and gathers the requested supporting facts.
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: A man and a woman sit side-by-side at a white marble kitchen island. The man, approximately 40-45 with dark skin, short black hair, and a trimmed beard, wears a dark navy button-down shirt. He holds a white document and a silver pen. The woman, mid-30s with a tan complexion and long dark wavy hair, wears a sage green blouse and leans in to look at the paper. A silver laptop is open on the left. A gray ceramic mug and a black binder sit in the foreground. The background is a bright kitchen with white subway tile and light wood shelves. Lighting is bright and natural from the left.

scenes.audio: This is field underwriting. It helps the insurer evaluate the risk, but it does not give the producer unlimited authority to approve coverage.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A clean motion graphic on a light beige background with a dark teal vertical bar on the far left. A white rectangular card labeled '01' with text appears on the left. A teal arrow points right as a second card labeled '02' appears. A third card labeled '03' follows. The lighting is flat and digital, with a palette of beige, teal, and white.

scenes.audio: The producer's report records relevant observations and transaction information truthfully. A blank answer is not automatically a no.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: The same graphic from the previous scene. The second white card is now highlighted with a thicker dark border while the others remain slightly dimmed. The background and layout are static.

scenes.audio: An unfamiliar medication is not a diagnosis the agent should invent. Ask for clarification and follow the carrier's approved procedure. Explain that underwriting and any temporary protection depend on their actual requirement.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: The graphic continues with the central card remaining highlighted. No camera movement. The overall color grading is warm and professional.

scenes.audio: Elena notices that the application lists the wrong medication date; correct it through the insurer's approved process and obtain the required acknowledgment.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: A new graphic screen appears with a different title at the top. Below the title, a list of four numbered items (01, 02, 03, 04) begins to appear one by one. Each item consists of a short title and a one-line description on a white rectangular card background. The teal sidebar remains on the left.

scenes.audio: Never erase a material answer secretly after signature or ask a client to sign a blank form for later completion. Verify the proposed insured, owner, and other required signatures, and each person's authority.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The graphic remains on screen. The text in the fourth card is now highlighted. The background maintains a high depth of field focus on the central cards.

scenes.audio: When more than one person completes a Maryland application, the signature area must identify the portion to which each signature applies. A lawful electronic signature process can be used when accepted.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The same graphic. The animation focuses on the final point regarding electronic signatures. The lighting is soft and even across the digital elements.

scenes.audio: Convenience does not authorize signing someone else's name. Maryland treats statements in a life application as representations, not warranties.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: A new graphic screen transitions in with a fresh title header. Three white cards appear in a row horizontally. Each card has a specific header and short explanatory text. The first card on the left is currently highlighted.

scenes.audio: Health questions must use the applicant's knowledge and belief standard or include the required representation statement. That does not make false answers harmless.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The graphic from the previous scene continues. The highlight shifts from the left card to the middle card. No camera movement or changes in lighting.

scenes.audio: Under Maryland law, a fraudulent or material misstatement can affect recovery. An agent should record the truth and refer an uncertain answer for clarification, not coach the applicant to hide it.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The graphic remains static with the third card on the right now highlighted. The background is a consistent cream color.

scenes.audio: The applicant should understand what information may be collected, how it may be used, and the rights described in the applicable notice.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: A new graphic screen appears with another title header. Three cards titled 'Notice', 'Authorization', and 'HIV testing' appear horizontally. The 'Notice' card is highlighted.

scenes.audio: Giving an information practices notice is not the same as obtaining every required authorization. If underwriting calls for an HIV test, use the appropriate informed-consent and confidentiality process.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The same graphic continues. The highlight moves to the second card 'Authorization' and then to the third card 'HIV testing'.

scenes.audio: Explain the current carrier forms, collect only relevant information through authorized channels, and protect it from unnecessary disclosure.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The graphic remains on screen. The layout is static as the audio finishes describing the carrier forms and information collection.

scenes.audio: An applicant wants a large cash value policy, seems unconcerned about protection, and asks how quickly an unrelated person can receive a surrender payment.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Transition to a new graphic screen with a title about money movements. A horizontal row of three cards labeled '01', '02', and '03' appears. Card '01' is highlighted.

scenes.audio: This combination calls for the insurer's anti-money laundering review. The federal insurance rule focuses on covered products, including individual permanent life and annuities.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The graphic continues. The second card '02' is now highlighted. The overall color palette remains consistent with teal accents.

scenes.audio: The insurer must integrate relevant agents and brokers into its program. Follow training, identity, and customer information procedures, document the facts, and escalate concerns.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The graphic continues. The third card '03' is highlighted. The text within the card points to internal escalation.

scenes.audio: Do not promise confidentiality that would defeat a required report.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Final segment of the money movement graphic. No movement. All cards are visible.

scenes.audio: Before submission, check the plan, amount, riders, ownership, beneficiary information, answers, signatures, notices, and any premium receipt.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Return to the man and woman from Scene 1 in the kitchen. They are in the same clothing. The man points to the paper with his pen as they both review it carefully. The lighting is still bright and natural.

scenes.audio: Tell Marcus what additional underwriting evidence may be needed. A submitted application is not the same as an issued policy or a promise of immediate coverage.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Transition to a final graphic screen with a new title. Four numbered cards (01-04) appear in a vertical list. The first and second cards are currently the focus.

scenes.audio: If a consumer report contributes to an adverse decision, the required notice identifies the reporting agency and explains the consumer's report and dispute rights.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: The graphic continues. The third card is highlighted. The background is static beige with the teal sidebar on the left.

scenes.audio: Help the applicant follow the review process while protecting privacy. Never solve a disappointing result by changing facts or hiding another application.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: The final graphic remains on screen, focusing on the last point. The screen fades slightly toward the end of the audio.
